Synopsis:
    A U.S. appeals court (1st Circuit) blocked the Trump administration's attempt to enforce a new USPS rule imposing stricter mail-in voting requirements ahead of November 2026 congressional elections. The rule — requiring states to share ballot recipient lists and mandating unique barcodes on ballot envelopes, with USPS empowered to refuse non-compliant ballots — stems from a March executive order. The injunction blocking the rule stands for now, but the matter escalates to the Supreme Court (6-3 conservative majority), which has already lifted an earlier injunction once. The outcome could affect mail ballot delivery for millions of voters before November.
